fields.detail: Directive 57 item 2, theorem_prover, only after test-dyadic-periodicity-prediction holds. State and prove, from Lucas alone and prime-free: for h eventually periodic with period 2^k, nu2(q_n) = O_k(1). Mechanism: by rule90-interior-xor the depth-d diagonal cell is an XOR of h over a binomial window with weights C(d,j) mod 2, and by Lucas those weights are supported on the binary submasks of d, so period-2^k h collapses the sums for all large d. This explains every counterexample (consecutive odds = period 1; alternating 2/4 = period 2) and sharpens the open supply bound into a precise question: which anti-dyadic property of the prime halved-gap bit string delivers nu2 >= c*n? Post the outcome to the board either way, including a refutation.
